steps: The runtime object panel shows two independent instances from real Bevy ECS. Stable instance and definition queries are read-only; unknown host/path/Entity fields and foreign jobs are rejected, and polling preserves the local filter.

The instance control action replays four real engine steps. Positions/states are sampled after each step; malformed local JSON and invalid/window HTTP controls start no job. Explicit target/example controls preserve edited JSON until the user requests an example; target, program text and caret survive refresh.

The real browser checks the saved plan, builds a data-only Bevy artifact, and runs a real App/ECS smoke step. Independent replay routes opposite and interleaved inputs to two instances of the same OC; omitted input releases the instance immediately, with final positions [200,220] and [490,210].
The unsupported window action stays disabled. A manually submitted HTTP window request is independently rejected with 422 before starting a job.
Chinese, English and Japanese show both runtime instances, translated states and explicit final-position sample labels at 390px without horizontal overflow. Window preview remains disabled.
An observed instance source link opens its frozen scene declaration; reopening the workbench retains the same owned run and both instances.
An unsaved scene-source draft blocks checks, builds and runs. Closing the workbench preserves draft text and caret, and every author file remains byte identical.
A separate default Godot HTTP host builds and runs the same source, then replays the same control program, then returns the same runtime object view and definition query as the Bevy host.
limitations: The browser uses a real local HTTP service. Packaged Tauri IPC and Android UI are not exercised.
The Bevy runtime exercises real App/ECS logic with controlled smoke input. Rendering, hardware keyboard input and GPU execution are not tested or advertised.
No author Rust behavior source is compiled or executed in this backend.
